items.prompt: In this food chain, what does the caterpillar eat?

figure.alt: Food chain: leaf, arrow, caterpillar, arrow, bird.

options.why: The arrow goes from the caterpillar to the bird, so the bird eats the caterpillar.
The chain shows the caterpillar eating something else.
Every animal must eat. The arrow shows what it eats.

hints: Arrows point from the food to the eater.
Find the arrow that points to the caterpillar.
Where does that arrow start?
items.explanation: The arrow points from the leaf to the caterpillar. This means the caterpillar eats the leaf.

items.prompt: Every food chain starts with a green plant. A plant is called a ___ because it makes its own food.
hints: Plants make their own food.
Animals that eat are called consumers.
The word starts with p.
items.explanation: Plants are producers because they make their own food using light. Every food chain begins with a producer.

items.prompt: Put this rice field food chain in order, starting with the producer.
hints: The producer is the plant.
What eats rice plants in a field?
Which animal hunts the snake?
items.explanation: Rats eat rice plants, snakes eat rats and eagles eat snakes. So the chain is rice plant, rat, snake, eagle.

items.prompt: What does an arrow in a food chain show?

options.why: Arrows have nothing to do with size.

options.text: the direction the food and energy go
which animals live next to each other
options.why: Arrows do not show where animals live.

options.text: which way the animal is facing
options.why: Arrows do not show which way an animal faces.

hints: An arrow points from one living thing to another.
It points from the food to the eater.
What moves along the chain when one thing eats another?
items.explanation: An arrow points from the food to the eater. It shows food and energy passing along the chain.

items.prompt: Look at this food chain. Which animal is both a predator and prey?

figure.alt: Food chain: seeds, arrow, mouse, arrow, snake, arrow, owl.

options.why: Nothing eats the owl in this chain. It is the top predator.
The mouse is prey, but it does not hunt animals here.
Seeds come from a plant. They are the producer.

hints: A predator hunts other animals.
Prey is hunted by another animal.
Find an animal that eats an animal and is eaten too.
items.explanation: The snake hunts the mouse, so it is a predator. The owl eats the snake, so the snake is also prey.

items.prompt: Match each word to its meaning.
pairs: makes its own food using light
gets energy by eating other living things
an animal that is hunted and eaten
hints: Two words are about how a living thing gets food.
Two words are about hunting.
Start with producer. What does a plant make?
items.explanation: Producers make food using light and consumers eat other living things. Predators hunt prey, and prey are the animals that get eaten.

items.prompt: Look at the food chain grass → rabbit → fox. What happens first if all the foxes disappear?

options.text: The number of rabbits goes down.
options.why: Foxes eat rabbits. With no foxes, fewer rabbits are eaten.
Grass would be eaten more over time, but not all at once.
Removing one living thing affects the others in its chain.

options.text: The number of rabbits goes up.

hints: Foxes eat rabbits.
Think about what stops eating the rabbits.
Would more or fewer rabbits survive?
items.explanation: With no foxes, fewer rabbits get eaten, so their numbers go up. Later, more rabbits would eat more grass.

options.why: Goats eat plants. They are consumers.
Mushrooms cannot make food from light, so they are not producers.
Frogs eat insects. They are consumers.

hints: Producers make their own food using light.
Producers are usually green.
Check each one: could it make food in sunlight?
items.explanation: Mango trees and seaweed use light to make food, so they are producers. Mushrooms, goats and frogs must get food from other living things.

items.prompt: Where does the energy in every food chain first come from?

options.why: Soil gives plants water and minerals. The energy comes from sunlight.
The top predator is at the end of the chain, not the start.
Living things need water, but it does not give them energy.

hints: Every food chain starts with a plant.
Plants need something to make their food.
What do leaves catch?
items.explanation: Plants use energy from sunlight to make food. That energy passes along the chain when animals eat.

items.prompt: How many consumers are in this food chain?

figure.alt: Food chain: pond weed, arrow, tadpole, arrow, fish, arrow, heron.

hints: Consumers eat other living things.
The pond weed is a producer.
Count every living thing after the pond weed.
items.explanation: The tadpole, fish and heron all eat other living things, so there are 3 consumers. The pond weed is the producer.

items.prompt: In a rice field, snakes eat rats and rats eat rice. People catch all the snakes. What happens to the rice?

options.text: The rice grows better, because snakes ate rice.
options.why: Snakes do not eat rice. They eat rats.

options.text: More rice is eaten, because there are more rats.

options.why: Removing snakes changes the number of rats, which affects the rice.

options.text: All the rats leave the field.
options.why: With no snakes, rats are safer, so they stay.

hints: Snakes eat rats.
Without snakes, what happens to the number of rats?
What do rats eat?
items.explanation: With no snakes, more rats survive. More rats eat more rice, so farmers lose more of their crop.

items.prompt: The table shows what each animal eats. If all the grasshoppers die, which animal loses food first?

head: Animal
Eats
figure.alt: Table of what animals eat: grasshopper eats grass, rabbit eats grass, frog eats grasshoppers, snake eats frogs and rabbits, eagle eats snakes.

options.why: Rabbits eat grass, not grasshoppers.
Eagles eat snakes. They may be affected later, not first.
Snakes eat frogs and rabbits. They are affected later.

hints: Find the animals that eat grasshoppers.
Read the Eats column.
Which animal eats only grasshoppers?
items.explanation: Frogs eat grasshoppers, so they lose their food first. Snakes might be affected later, but they can still eat rabbits.

items.prompt: Draw a food chain with a producer and three consumers. Draw the arrows the right way.

criteria.label: Arrows point from the food to the eater
Labels the producer and the consumers

hints: Start with a green plant.
Each arrow means is eaten by.
items.explanation: A food chain starts with a plant. Each arrow points from the living thing that is eaten to the one that eats it.
